surprises.description: CMS’s reported year-to-date adjusted EPS of $2.95, against the preview’s already-reported H1 EPS of $1.50, implies Q3 EPS of about $1.45—far above the $1.16 consensus estimate. That is roughly a 25% beat, well above even the preview’s bull-case range.
surprises.fact_evidence: The call reported “year-to-date adjusted EPS reached $2.95.” The preview reported H1 adjusted EPS of $1.50, implying Q3 adjusted EPS of approximately $1.45.

surprises.description: CMS reported about 745 MW of new load contracts, with roughly 450 MW already energized, excluding a separately signed large data center. That is substantially more than the approximately 110 MW signed YTD as of Q2 that the preview cited, and exceeds the preview’s bull-case trigger of converting 1–2 GW in final-stage negotiations into a signed contract only if a new data-center deal closed.
surprises.fact_evidence: CMS had “signed approximately 745 MW of new load contracts (about 450 MW already energized),” excluding “a separately signed large data center.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Only ~110 MW was signed YTD as of Q2”; the bull case looked for “1–2 GW ‘final stage’ load” to convert to signed.

surprises.description: The call disclosed projected financial compensation from the PPA mechanism of about $125 million in 2031, rising to roughly $195 million by 2040, with more than 70% of 2031 contracts already signed or online. The preview did not identify this earnings-related mechanism or its projected contribution.
surprises.fact_evidence: The PPA financial compensation mechanism is projected at “approximately $125 million in 2031, growing to about $195 million by 2040,” with “over 70% of 2031 contracts already signed or online.”

surprises.description: CMS reported commission approval of a $139 million gas rate increase, about 60% of its request, at a 9.8% ROE. The preview focused on the electric rate case and did not flag this gas-rate decision, so there was no stated expectation for the outcome.
surprises.fact_evidence: The Michigan commission “approved a $139 million gas rate increase (about 60% of the ask) with a 9.8% ROE and 50% equity ratio.”

surprises.description: CMS disclosed that it may pull forward refinancing of approximately $625 million of parent debt due next year. The preview discussed 2026 equity funding and the capital plan but did not anticipate this possible timing change; the call did not indicate whether it would change financing costs or the amount of funding required.
surprises.fact_evidence: CMS “may pull forward refinancing of the approximately $625 million of parent debt maturing next year.”

surprises.description: The call put the IRP’s long-term capital opportunities at roughly $27 billion, a concrete opportunity figure beyond the preview’s discussion of a $24 billion-plus five-year plan. The preview said an early preview of an IRP-driven plan upsize could be positive, but the call described opportunities rather than confirming a larger committed capital plan.
surprises.fact_evidence: The IRP “outlines roughly $27 billion in long-term capital opportunities,” including clean energy, battery storage, and new gas generation.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “$24bn+ five-year plan”; the IRP “sets up a plan upsize—most likely at the Q4/February update, but a preview here would be a positive surprise.”
